archetype: Adding a dark mode to a design system consumed by a web app and two embedded widgets that ship on different cadences
title: Implement Dark Mode Tokens for Core System and Embedded Widgets
ticket: Our customers are reporting eye strain when using the Acme Portal at night, and our enterprise partners want their embedded widgets to match their own dark themes. We need you to extend our current design system to support a full dark mode palette. This isn't just a CSS swap; the new tokens must work seamlessly in the main web application and both the Sales and Support embedded widgets. Please ensure the contrast ratios meet our updated accessibility standards without breaking the existing light mode. The widgets ship on different schedules than the main app, so the solution must be backward compatible until everyone upgrades. Let's aim to have this ready for the next quarterly review.
repo_context: The design system lives in the 'acme-core' monorepo, consumed by the main portal and two separate widget repositories via a private package registry. CI pipelines for the widgets run on shared infrastructure with a strict thirty-minute timeout; complex visual regression suites often hit this limit, causing false failures that require manual retry by the Platform Team. Only Senior Staff Engineers can approve changes to the shared token configuration file, as an erroneous push there breaks builds for all three consuming applications instantly. Note that the Support Widget still runs on a legacy rendering engine that does not support dynamic theme switching, requiring a static fallback asset generation step during its specific build process.

archetype: Replacing a nightly full database dump with incremental backups while a compliance audit is open
title: Switch to Incremental Backups During Audit
ticket: We are currently under a strict compliance audit for the Mercury Ledger system, and our nightly full database dumps are causing unacceptable latency during business hours. The auditors have flagged our recovery time objectives as borderline, but they explicitly forbade any change to the retention policy until the review closes next month. I need you to implement an incremental backup strategy that runs every four hours without altering the existing daily full snapshot schedule yet. Please ensure the new process logs verification checksums to the compliance ledger automatically. Do not delete the old full dump scripts; we must maintain the ability to revert immediately if the auditors request a demonstration of the original workflow. This is urgent.
repo_context: The Mercury Ledger backend resides in the 'ledger-core' monorepo, managed by the Data Integrity team. Production deploys require dual approval from the CTO and the external compliance officer via the change management portal. Our CI pipeline costs $45 per run and takes 55 minutes, so frequent test iterations are discouraged. A known flaky check in the network latency suite often fails falsely on Tuesdays due to maintenance windows. The database credentials are rotated automatically every Friday at midnight by a shared cron job owned by the Security team; modifying this cron will break authentication. Additionally, the audit log storage is immutable; once written, entries cannot be edited or removed, making test data pollution irreversible.

archetype: Enabling HTTP/2 or a new TLS version at a load balancer shared by several teams' services
title: Enable TLS 1.3 on Atlas Load Balancer
ticket: We need to upgrade the Atlas shared load balancer to support TLS 1.3 immediately. Our security audit flagged our current configuration as non-compliant for the upcoming fiscal year. Several downstream services, including the billing gateway and user portal, depend on this termination point. Please coordinate the rollout during the Tuesday maintenance window. We cannot afford downtime, so a blue-green swap is mandatory. Ensure all teams have validated their certificates against the new protocol before we flip the switch. I need confirmation that rollback procedures are tested and ready, as any handshake failures will block customer transactions globally.
repo_context: The Atlas load balancer configuration lives in the central network-ops repository, shared by twelve product teams. CI pipelines take forty-five minutes to run full integration suites due to expensive synthetic traffic generation, costing two hundred credits per run. The 'certificate-validation' check is known to flake intermittently when network latency spikes, requiring manual re-triggers. Only the Senior Network Architect, Jane Smith, can approve merges to the main branch. Production changes require a dual-sign-off from both the Security Lead and the Platform Director. Reverting a protocol change triggers an automatic freeze on all deployments for one hour, making errors highly irreversible during business hours.

archetype: A webhook signature scheme change that integrators must adopt before the old scheme is switched off
title: Migrate Webhook Signatures to v2 Scheme
ticket: Our external partners are failing validation because we are still sending events signed with the legacy v1 algorithm. The security team has mandated that we switch to the new v2 signature scheme by the end of the month, as the old keys will be revoked immediately after. Please update the event dispatcher to generate the new hash format and ensure the payload structure matches the updated integration guide. We cannot afford any downtime during this transition, so you must implement a feature flag to toggle between schemes. Verify that our top three integrators can successfully validate the new signatures in the staging environment before we enable this globally. This is critical for maintaining our compliance certification.
repo_context: The notification service lives in the 'acme-events' monorepo, sharing a common crypto library with the billing module that cannot be modified without finance approval. Our continuous integration pipeline takes forty-five minutes to run full regression suites due to heavy data seeding, and the external sandbox environment is only available between 2 AM and 5 AM UTC to avoid load testing conflicts. Deployments to production require explicit sign-off from both the Lead Architect and the Security Officer. Note that the legacy signature logic is tightly coupled with the audit logging system; changing the hash input format inadvertently breaks log indexing, so you must update the log parser simultaneously. Reverting a failed deployment requires a manual database rollback which is irreversible for processed event states.

archetype: Introducing a service mesh sidecar into a cluster where a few pods are latency-critical
title: Deploy sidecar proxy to non-critical namespaces only
ticket: We need to start rolling out the new network proxy sidecar to improve observability, but I am extremely worried about latency spikes. Please configure the automation to inject the sidecar only into the 'billing-reporting' and 'audit-log' namespaces immediately. Do not touch the 'real-time-trading' or 'user-checkout' pods yet; those are too sensitive for this initial phase. I need a report by Friday confirming that the sidecar is running in the target namespaces without increasing error rates. If you see any CPU throttling alerts, roll back the change automatically. We cannot afford even a millisecond of added delay for our core transaction services during market hours.
repo_context: The cluster runs across three availability zones with manual promotion gates requiring approval from two senior architects. The continuous integration pipeline takes 45 minutes to complete security scanning and costs $12 per execution, so avoid triggering unnecessary rebuilds. A known flaky check in the network policy validator often fails intermittently; engineers currently retry it twice before investigating. The shared configuration file 'global-mesh-policy.yaml' is locked during business hours to prevent conflicting edits. Once the sidecar image is published to the production registry, the action is irreversible without a full cluster restore. The 'real-time-trading' team maintains a separate, frozen configuration branch that must not be merged.

archetype: Consolidating two customer-support ticket systems into one while open tickets keep receiving replies
title: Merge Legacy Support Portals with Live Sync
ticket: We are retiring the old 'HelpDesk Alpha' portal and moving everything to 'SupportCentral'. The hard part is that customers are still emailing into both systems right now. I need a solution that ingests new replies from Alpha into Central in real-time without creating duplicate threads or losing attachment history. We cannot pause incoming traffic for the migration. Please ensure that when an agent updates a ticket in Central, the sender on Alpha gets the notification automatically. Do not close any open cases during the switch; they must remain editable in the new system immediately after transfer.
repo_context: The codebase lives in the 'unified-care' monorepo, managed by the Platform Team. Production deploys require sign-off from both the Security Lead and the VP of Operations. Our CI pipeline costs $45 per run and averages 28 minutes; frequent retries trigger budget alerts. A known flaky check exists in the notification module that falsely fails 15% of the time but is ignored by senior devs. The database schema is shared with the billing service, so locking tables for migration is strictly forbidden. Additionally, the staging environment lacks the legacy email gateway, making end-to-end testing of inbound replies impossible locally.

archetype: Adding GDPR-style data export and delete endpoints to a service whose data is spread across five stores
title: Implement GDPR Data Export and Deletion Endpoints
ticket: Our legal team requires immediate compliance with new data privacy regulations. We need two new endpoints on the user profile service: one to generate a complete archive of all personal data associated with an account, and another to permanently wipe that data. The challenge is that user information is currently fragmented across five distinct storage systems. You must ensure the export aggregates everything into a single readable format and the deletion removes records from every location without leaving orphaned entries. Please prioritize data consistency; if the deletion fails midway, we cannot have partial removes. The compliance officer needs this deployed before the end of the month to avoid regulatory fines.
repo_context: The user profile service is owned by the Identity Squad and deploys to three isolated environments via a manual approval gate from the Security Lead. Our continuous integration pipeline costs significant credits per run and takes forty-five minutes to complete due to heavy integration tests against live legacy databases. A known flaky check exists in the network latency suite that often requires manual retry. The database schema is shared with the billing microservice, so direct migrations are prohibited without a joint review. Furthermore, the deletion operation is irreversible once committed to the primary store, and our backup retention policy only keeps snapshots for seven days, making testing on production-like data extremely risky.

archetype: Swapping the image-resizing library in a media pipeline where output must stay byte-stable for cache keys
title: Replace Image Resizer in Media Pipeline with Byte-Stable Output
ticket: We need to swap out our current image-resizing library in the media processing pipeline because it's causing intermittent cache invalidations. The new library must produce byte-for-byte identical outputs for the same inputs to ensure our cache keys remain stable. Please verify that all existing unit and integration tests pass, and confirm that no downstream services experience disruptions. This change is critical for reducing our CDN costs, which have spiked due to unnecessary re-processing. Ensure the deployment includes a rollback plan in case we see any anomalies in production metrics.
repo_context: The media pipeline resides in the 'acme-media-core' repository, managed by the Platform Engineering team. CI pipelines take approximately 45 minutes to complete due to extensive image processing tests, and each run incurs a significant cloud cost. The staging environment mirrors production but uses a smaller dataset to expedite testing. Deployments require approval from both the lead engineer and the SRE on-call. A known flaky check exists in the thumbnail generation module, which sometimes fails without affecting overall functionality. The current library is deeply embedded in shared utility files used by three other microservices, making isolation challenging.

archetype: Changing the primary key type of a heavily written table from integer to UUID
title: Migrate Orders Table Primary Key to UUID
ticket: Our Orders table is hitting integer limits and causing collision risks during regional merges. We need to switch the primary key from a standard integer to a UUID format immediately. This change must preserve all existing historical data and maintain zero downtime for our global checkout flow. Please ensure that all downstream reporting jobs and the legacy billing adapter, which currently assume numeric IDs, are updated to handle the new string format. We cannot afford any data loss or extended maintenance windows, so a blue-green migration strategy is required. Verify that the new keys generate correctly across all three availability zones before enabling traffic.
repo_context: The Orders service resides in the monolithic 'CoreCommerce' repository, managed by the Platform Team. CI pipelines take 45 minutes to complete due to heavy integration testing against a 2TB production snapshot, costing $120 per run. The database is a shared cluster where schema locks longer than 30 seconds trigger automatic failovers. Deployment requires dual approval from the Lead Architect and the Data Governance Officer. Note that the 'daily-reconciliation' batch job hardcodes integer parsing logic in a shared library used by five other services; changing this breaks the audit trail irreversibly if not coordinated. Flaky network checks in the staging environment often false-negative during high-load simulations.

archetype: Adding SSO login for enterprise tenants without breaking existing password users
title: Enable SSO for Enterprise Tenants Alongside Legacy Auth
ticket: We need to roll out Single Sign-On for our new Enterprise tier customers without disrupting the standard username and password flow for our existing Small Business users. The goal is to allow Enterprise admins to enforce identity provider rules while keeping legacy accounts fully functional. Please ensure the login page dynamically selects the correct method based on the tenant configuration. We cannot afford any downtime or forced logouts for current users during this transition. The feature must be hidden behind a feature flag until we verify stability in the staging environment with our pilot customer, Globex Corp.
repo_context: The authentication logic resides in the shared 'core-identity' module used by both the web portal and mobile API. Our continuous integration pipeline takes 45 minutes to complete full regression suites due to heavy database seeding, costing significant compute credits per run. The staging environment mirrors production data structure but uses a mock identity provider that occasionally times out, causing flaky test failures in the login stream. Deployments to production require explicit written approval from the Security Lead and the VP of Product. Note that modifying the legacy session cookie format is irreversible without a full user reset, so backward compatibility is mandatory.
